subject: gk
question: Which of the following situations will result in a point awarded to the defending team in Kabaddi?

options.text: The raider tags two defenders and crosses the midliners
The raider fails to chant "Kabaddi" during the raid
The raider touches the bonus line without being tackled
The defending team crosses the lobby before contact

solution:
The correct answer is __**The raider fails to chant "Kabaddi" during the raid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sport of **Kabaddi**, the **"Cant"** is the continuous clear chanting of the approved word **"Kabaddi"** by the **raider** in a single breath. If the raider fails to maintain this chant or loses their breath during the **raid**, they are declared **out**, and the **defending team** is awarded **1 point**. *Hence, statement B is correct.*
 
• When a **raider** successfully tags or touches **two defenders** and safely returns to their own half by crossing the **midline**, the **raiding team** is awarded **2 points** (one for each defender touched), and those defenders must leave the mat. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• Touching the **bonus line** is a specific scoring maneuver. If a **raider** crosses the **bonus line** with one foot while the other foot is in the air, and there are **6 or 7 defenders** present on the mat, the **raiding team** receives **1 point**. This does not result in a point for the defense. *Hence, statement C is incorrect.*
 
• The **lobby** area (the yellow strips on the sides) only becomes **"active"** once a touch has been made between the **raider** and a **defender**. If a defender steps into the **lobby** without any contact being initiated, they are considered **"out of bounds,"** and a point is awarded to the **raiding team**. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*
 
• According to the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)** rules, a **raid** is unsuccessful if the raider is tackled, goes out of bounds, or commits a **technical foul** like losing the **cant**. In all these cases, the **defending team** earns a point and revives one of their own players.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Court Dimensions and Player Count:** A standard **Kabaddi** court for **men** measures **13 meters by 10 meters**, while for **women** and **juniors**, it is **12 meters by 8 meters**. Each team consists of **12 players**, but only **7 players** are allowed on the **mat** at any given time during the match.
 
• **Super Tackle:** This is a unique scoring rule where if the **defending team** has **3 or fewer defenders** on the mat and they successfully tackle the **raider**, they are awarded **2 points** instead of the usual 1. This is a crucial strategy in modern leagues like the **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)**, which began in **2014**.
 
• **Lobby Rule:** The **lobby** is the **1-meter wide** strip on both sides of the court. It is considered part of the playing area only during a **struggle** (after a touch). If a player enters it without a touch, they are **eliminated** from the current round.
 
• **Duration of Match:** A professional match typically lasts for **40 minutes**, divided into two halves of **20 minutes** each, with a **5-minute break** in between. In the **Asian Games**, where **Kabaddi** has been a regular feature since **1990**, these timing rules are strictly followed.
 
• **Types of Kabaddi:** There are two main styles: the **Standard Style** (played on a rectangular mat) and the **Circle Style** (played on a circular field, popular in **Punjab**). The **Pro Kabaddi League** and **World Cup** follow the **Standard Style**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Do-or-Die Raid:** If a team performs **two consecutive empty raids** (raids where no points are scored or lost), the **third raid** is designated as a **"Do-or-Die" raid**. In this raid, the **raider** must score a point (by touch or bonus), or they will be declared **out**, even if they are not tackled.
 
• **Raid Time Limit:** Every **raid** has a maximum duration of **30 seconds**. If the **raider** fails to return to their half within this **30-second** window, they are ruled **out**, and the **defending team** receives a point.
 
• **All-Out (Lona):** When a team manages to eliminate all **7 players** of the opposing team, they score an **"All-Out,"** which awards **2 bonus points** in addition to the points earned for the individual touches. All eliminated players of the opposing team are then **revived**.
 
• **Technical Points:** Points can also be awarded for **coaching violations**, **wrong substitutions**, or if a defender pulls the **raider's hair** or clothes. These are called **technical points** and do not result in the **revival** of a player.
